question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f$ as the composite function

$$
f={6}^{u},\,u=-3{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}={6}^{u}\ln(6),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={6}^{u}\ln(6)\cdot (-6x) \\ & =(-6x)\cdot {6}^{u}\ln(6) \\ & =-6x\cdot {6}^{-3{x}^{2}}\ln(6).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=0} & =(-8)\cdot {4}^{-1-4(0)}\ln(4) \\ & =-8\cdot {4}^{-1}\ln(4) \\ & =- 2 \ln{\left(4 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=0$ is $- 2 \ln{\left(4 \right)}.$
